correctness.rationale: For r>=2 and t>=1 set Q=2^(2r), b=Q-3*2^(r-1), c=b-Q/2+1, x=c-1, y=b+1. Direct blockwise reverse-complement identities show both explicit B=[b,x^t,c,y^t,b]_Q and A=[b-1,Q/2,0^(t-1),1,Q/2-1,(Q-1)^(t-1),Q-2,Q-b]_Q are canonical binary antipalindromes. Base-Q borrowing establishes A=(Q-1)B, with denominator length exactly 2r(2t+3), strictly increasing in t. The base cases t=1 and r=2 have no empty-block ambiguity. Independently evaluated 56 cases with a separate exact-integer construction. The unbounded claim rests on symbolic identities, not finite experiments.

value.rationale: Infinite representation multiplicity is a primary mathematical question for binary-antipalindromic quotients. The natural odd Mersenne family is separated by a genuine multiplicity transition from the neighboring 4^r+1 family. A single infinite construction uniform in r, not a table lookup or trivial arithmetic substitution, has independent mathematical use.

limitations: Does not classify all antipalindromic quotient integers or enumerate every representation of 4^r-1.
